extracted.intended_audience: LTCH and PCH quality reporting staff, hospital administrators, and health IT developers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and technical requirements for submitting electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) and assessment data, measure removal and public reporting policies, and related CEHRT certification impacts for Long-Term Care Hospitals (LTCHs) and Psychiatric Centers for Hospitals (PCHs).

rubrics_metrics.name: QRDA Category I (QRDA I) file format requirement for eCQM submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that a PCH must submit eCQM data via the QRDA Category I (QRDA I) file format; a PCH may use third parties to submit QRDA I files on their behalf; a PCH may either use abstraction or pull the data from non-certified sources to then input these data into certified health IT for capture and reporting in the QRDA I file format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QRDA is the standard file format used for eCQM submission in CMS programs that rely on QRDA-based eCQM reporting. For technical guidance, the rule refers readers to the QRDA Implementation Guides at https://ecqi.healthit.gov/qrda/versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: QRDA I file patient-per-file and five key identification elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that QRDA I files reflect data for one patient per file per quarter and contain five key elements necessary to identify the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five key elements are: (1) CCN; (2) CMS Program Name; (3) EHR Patient ID; (4) Reporting period specified in the Reporting Parameters Section; and (5) EHR Submitter ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero denominator declaration as acceptable submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PCH's health IT is certified to an eCQM but the PCH does not have patients that meet the denominator criteria of that eCQM, the PCH would submit a zero in the denominator for that eCQM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a zero in the denominator for such an eCQM would qualify as a successful submission for that eCQM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case threshold exemption policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to allow a PCH using certified health IT to be exempt from reporting on an eCQM if the PCH does not meet the case threshold of applicable inpatient encounters/discharges for the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically proposed thresholds: 5 or fewer applicable inpatient encounters or discharges per quarter, or 20 or fewer applicable inpatient encounters or discharges per year (Medicare and non‑Medicare combined). Exemptions would be entered on the Denominator Declaration screen in CMS' Hospital Quality Reporting System; the exemption is optional (a PCH may instead report individual cases); measures with counts below the case threshold would not have their measure rate publicly reported. Applicability is defined by each eCQM's denominator specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM submission deadline (calendar-year alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require eCQM data submission for the PCH Quality Reporting Program by the end of 2 months following the close of the calendar year for the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 program year and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for CY 2028 reporting period, PCHs would be required to submit by February 28, 2029. If the date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day. This aligns with existing program deadlines to minimize burden and simplify understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and corrections period for eCQM data
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to have a review and corrections period for eCQM data that runs concurrently with the data submission period (from the time submission opens until the submission deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Hospital Quality Reporting System, providers can submit QRDA Category I test and production data files and correct these files before production data are submitted for final reporting. The system does not allow data to be submitted or corrected after the annual deadline. CMS encourages early testing and use of pre-submission testing tools and refers to HQR, eCQI Resource Center, and CMS QualityNet for resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure removal Factor 3: does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the factors used under §412.560(b)(3) to evaluate removal of measures: a measure does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites this Factor 3 as the basis for proposing removal of COVID-19 vaccination measures where CDC guidance has shifted to shared clinical decision-making and the original population-level vaccination expectations no longer apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to remove COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among Healthcare Personnel (HCP) measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove the HCP COVID-19 Vaccine measure from the LTCH QRP beginning with the FY 2028 LTCH QRP under removal Factor 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes end of the Public Health Emergency, decreased COVID-19 death rates, changes in CDC recommendations toward shared clinical decision-making, and burdens of reporting that outweigh benefits. CMS notes prior removal of this measure from multiple other quality reporting programs. If finalized, LTCHs would not be required to report CY 2026 data for FY 2028 determinations and any CY 2026 data received would not be used for compliance or public reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to remove COVID-19 Vaccine: Percent of Patients/Residents Who Are Up to Date measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove the Patient/Resident COVID-19 Vaccine measure from the LTCH QRP beginning with the FY 2028 LTCH QRP under removal Factor 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: CDC guidance for 2025-2026 is based on shared clinical decision-making so being 'up to date' may be consistent with both vaccination and nonvaccination; thus the measure may no longer provide information on prevalence of vaccination. CMS proposes that beginning with discharges on or after Oct 1, 2026 LTCHs would no longer be required to collect and submit the measure; the data element O0350 would be removed from the LCDS as of Oct 1, 2028 (becomes voluntary in the interim). Public reporting would end after the September 2026 Care Compare refresh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for selecting LTCH QRP measures / advanced care planning RFI priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is seeking input on importance, relevance, appropriateness, and applicability of advanced care planning as a quality measure concept for the LTCH QRP and will prioritize evidence-based outcome measures that promote person-centered care practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance care planning guidance: continuous process, supports understanding and communicating goals/values/preferences, requires regular reassessment as condition changes, documents preferences to ensure goal‑concordant care across transitions. CMS will prioritize measures that are evidence-based and appropriate for the LTCH setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to revise LTCH QRP LCDS assessment data submission deadline to 15th day of second month after quarter end
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the FY 2029 LTCH QRP, proposal that LTCHs must complete their LCDS assessment data submissions and corrections no later than the 15th day of the second month after the end of the calendar quarter (with next-business-day adjustment if the date falls on a Friday, weekend, or Federal holiday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: reduce the approximately nine-month lag between data collection end and public reporting by up to three months, improving timeliness for consumers and quality improvement. CMS analysis using 2024 data showed ~98.36% of assessments already submitted within a 45-day timeframe, implying limited impact on most LTCHs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to revise LTCH QRP CDC NHSN data submission deadline to 15th day of second month after quarter end
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the FY 2029 LTCH QRP, proposal that LTCHs must complete their CDC NHSN data submissions and corrections no later than the 15th day of the second month after the end of the calendar quarter (with next-business-day adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale mirrors LCDS proposal; CMS analysis using FY 2025 data showed 88% of LTCHs already submitted CDC NHSN data within a 45-day timeframe. No change to the Influenza Vaccination Coverage among HCP measure deadline (remains May 15 for each influenza season).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to end public display of HCP COVID-19 Vaccine measure on Care Compare
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that, if the HCP COVID-19 Vaccine measure is removed, LTCH HCP COVID-19 measure data would be publicly reported for the last time with the September 2026 Care Compare refresh on Medicare.gov based on Q4 2025 data, and thereafter would not be displayed on Care Compare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS invites comment on ending public display of this measure following the specified refresh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to end public display of Patient/Resident COVID-19 Vaccine measure on Care Compare
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that if the Patient/Resident COVID-19 Vaccine measure is removed, its data would be publicly reported for the last time with the September 2026 Care Compare refresh on Medicare.gov and would not be displayed thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the proposal, the data element would be voluntary from Oct 1, 2026 through Sep 30, 2027 and removed from LCDS as of Oct 1, 2028; CMS invites comment on ending public display.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONC HTI-5 proposed removals/revisions to Health IT certification criteria impacting CEHRT
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of ONC's HTI-5 proposed rule identifying 34 certification criteria for removal and 7 for revision in the ONC Health IT Certification Program, and noting that these changes are relevant to eligible hospitals and CAHs participating in the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing or revising certification criteria could reduce burden and costs for developers and clinicians by decreasing necessity to maintain conformance. The proposed changes affect certification criteria included in the Base EHR definition at 45 CFR 170.102 (and thus CEHRT at 42 CFR 495.4), which may remove requirements that eligible hospitals or CAHs use CEHRT that includes certain functionalities. CMS summarized impacts in Table IX.F.-01 and cross-references other related proposals in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ONC certification criteria proposed for removal from Base EHR
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC proposed to remove specific certification criteria from the Base EHR definition, including: 45 CFR 170.315(a)(14) — 'implantable device list'; 45 CFR 170.315(h)(1) — 'transport methods and other protocols—Direct Project'; and 45 CFR 170.315(h)(2) — 'transport methods and other protocols—Direct Project, Edge Protocol, and XDR/XDM.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of these criteria from the Base EHR definition would remove the requirement that eligible hospitals or CAHs must use CEHRT that includes these functionalities for purposes of the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program. CMS links these ONC proposals to potential effects on the CEHRT definition in 42 CFR 495.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEHRT definition depends on Base EHR and criteria necessary to be a meaningful EHR user
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of Certified Electronic Health Record Technology (CEHRT) in 42 CFR 495.4 includes EHR technology certified under the ONC Health IT Certification Program that meets the Base EHR definition at 45 CFR 170.102 and technology certified to the criteria necessary to be a meaningful EHR user under the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria necessary to be a meaningful EHR user include those necessary to report on applicable objectives and measures under the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program. ONC HTI-5 proposals affecting Base EHR or other criteria can therefore change what functionality counts as CEHRT for program participation and reporting.
